column1: # Network-device firmware map: device -> driver -> firmware package -> where
# the blobs must land.  Read by build/iso/patch-initrd-t2-kernel.py (rows whose
# `where` contains "initrd" are copied out of the offline mirror's .deb into
# the d-i initrd at /lib/firmware) and by build/test-net-firmware.sh (every
# package named here must be in manifests/firmware.pkgs, which seeds the
# offline mirror and which post-install/13-firmware-bom.sh installs onto the
# target).
# Columns (TAB separated):
#   device    human-readable device family
#   driver    kernel driver that requests the blobs
#   package   Debian binary package that ships them
#   firmware  space-separated globs relative to /usr/lib/firmware; every glob
#             must match at least one file in the package or the build fails
#   where     initrd+target | target
# Why the initrd rows exist (2026-10-06): d-i ships no non-free firmware, so
# every Realtek NIC in the installer ran without its PHY/MCU patch
# (O6N: "Unable to load firmware rtl_nic/rtl8125b-2.fw (-2)", PEGASUS:
# rtl8168h-2.fw, MS-R1: rtl8127a-1.fw), and the MS-R1's MT7922 Bluetooth
# (btusb/btmtk) failed BT_RAM_CODE_MT7922_1_1_hdr.bin every ~0.4 s for the
# whole install, resetting the USB device each time and flooding the kernel
# ring buffer (it evicted the r8169 lines entirely).  r8169 requests its blob
# at ndo_open (rtl8169_open), not at probe, so a missing blob never removes
# the interface; it only leaves the PHY unpatched.
# WiFi blobs are deliberately target-only.  Giving d-i a working wlan
# interface changes netcfg's choose_interface=auto behaviour on a machine
# with no wired carrier (it can stop at the ESSID prompt in an unattended
# install).  The T2 Broadcom path is handled separately (post-install/
# 55-t2-firmware.sh on the target, from the same tarball).
# Apple T2 WiFi: firmware-brcm80211 does NOT carry the Apple board variants
# (brcmfmac4355c1 / 4364b2 / 4364b3 / 4377b3). Verified 2026-10-06 against
# firmware-brcm80211_20260810-1_all.deb: 0 hits for those names; the 113 files
# it does ship under brcm/ are all upstream boards. The T2 blobs are
# Apple-licensed and ship only in
# assets/firmware/apple-t2/apple-t2-firmware-sonoma14.tar.xz, so they cannot be
# a row here -- this table resolves `package` to a .deb in the offline mirror,
# and naming firmware-brcm80211 would bake 113 wrong-board blobs into d-i while
# the radio still could not associate.
# They DO reach d-i through a different, purpose-built path:
# build/iso/patch-initrd-firmware.py extracts the brcmfmac* blobs from that
# tarball into the initrd's lib/firmware/brcm/. build/build-installer-image.sh
# now calls it (wired 2026-10-06, before patch-initrd-t2-kernel.py so the two
# chain instead of overwriting each other). Keep these rows target-only; the
# initrd half is that script's job, not this table's.
# device
Realtek RTL8111/8168/8125/8126/8127 PCIe 1-10GbE (O6N 8125B, MS-R1 8127A, PEGASUS 8168H)
Realtek RTL8153/8156 USB 1-2.5GbE
MediaTek MT7922/MT7921(MT7961) Bluetooth (MS-R1 M.2)
MediaTek MT7922/MT7921(MT7961) WiFi (MS-R1 M.2)
MediaTek MT7925 WiFi+Bluetooth
Realtek RTW89 WiFi (8852BE/8852CE, Sky1 M.2)
Realtek RTW88 WiFi
Realtek Bluetooth (RTW88/RTW89 combo cards)
Intel AX2xx/BE2xx WiFi (amd64 laptops)
Broadcom/AMPAK WiFi (ARM SBC modules)
Qualcomm Atheros QCA6174/QCA9377
Qualcomm WCN6855/QCN9074
Qualcomm WCN7850
Intel integrated display DMC (Meteor/Arrow Lake etc.; PROTEUS i915 ran the installer with "Direct firmware load for i915/mtl_dmc.bin failed -2")
